messages:
jamie: Heads up — ACME says a large fraction of their streaming calls from our hosted API are being marked as 5xx and billed. They sent a few request IDs and say their client never aborted. Can we triage?

maria: Thanks, can you paste one of the request IDs and any stack/log snippets? Also which region and model?

jamie: req: req_20260315_acme_01 region: us-west-2 model: redwood-7b-chat. From the gateway logs: 
```
gateway: upstream write to socket failed: broken pipe (EPIPE)
upstream: connection half-closed by client, no trailer received
http: chunked transfer encoding: premature EOF
classification: labeled 5xx
```
They attached a pcap and client side library logs that show repeated TCP FIN followed by reconnects, but no explicit client error.

lee: Quick thought — our billing/metrics pipeline treats upstream abrupt EOFs (EPIPE) as 5xx by default. That heuristic historically covered server crashes. If client-initiated FIN arrives first we should not bill as a 5xx.

maria: Can we repro? jamie, can you share the exact client behaviour? A minimal repro would help (node/python snippet).

jamie: ACME devs said they do an aggressive connection reuse + idle socket probe. Their client will sometimes send FIN on an idle connection then re-open. They claim the sequence is: keepalive probe -> client halfclose -> server still streaming -> gateway observes "write failed: broken pipe" and marks 5xx. Repro snippet they used (Node):
```
// simplified repro
const http = require('http');
const req = http.request({ host: 'api.redwood.com', path: '/v1/stream', method: 'POST', headers: { 'Transfer-Encoding': 'chunked' } }, res => {
  res.on('data', d => process.stdout.write(d));
});
req.write('prompt chunk');
// immediately half-close socket
req.end(); // client thinks stream done but TCP FIN races with server chunk
// then client reconnects quickly
```
They say sometimes the gateway writes a chunk and then sees the FIN and raises EPIPE.

lee: That lines up. This is a race between our write path and a downstream FIN. Currently our gateway maps EPIPE and writes-after-halfclose to a 5xx and emits an event that increments billing counters. We should differentiate: if downstream FIN with no error payload/trailer, classify as client-abort and not bill.

maria: Agreed. Immediate mitigation: 1) update billing pipeline to mark those events as non-billable by query (we can reclassify historical 1h window for ACME), 2) short-term runtime tweak: swallow EPIPE if we detect TCP FIN from client within X ms of write (risky but okay as patch behind flag).

jamie: ACME needs a billing credit and a repro ticket. Can ops-bot create an incident? Tagging: @lee @maria.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-43210 — "streaming EPIPE misclassified as 5xx for connection reuse pattern". Priority: P2. Related logs attached.

lee: I'll put up a tiny change to the gateway classification in a feature branch: if socket shutdown is graceful (FIN) and no server-side exception, don't increment 5xx/billing meter. Will add feature flag and rollout to us-west-2 only first.

maria: I'll coordinate the billing reclassification script: target ACME's request IDs between 2026-03-15T09:00 and 2026-03-15T12:00, re-tag events as client_disconnect_nonbill. Need a support approval note to run against billing DB.

jamie: ACME confirmed they're okay with the partial workaround as long as we don't break correctness for real server errors. They provided 6 sample req IDs; dropping them in #private-ticket.

lee: Quick note on reproducibility: sometimes the race is timing-sensitive. A deterministic repro: on the client side, send FIN right before the server writes the final chunk (use a tiny sleep on server), or use tc qdisc to add 10-30ms delay to the server egress. That reliably surfaces the EPIPE path.

maria: Thanks. Action items:
- lee: feature branch for classification rule + FF (eta: 4h to PR, 24h to canary)
- maria: billing reclass script + run after legal/finance thumbs (eta: 2 business days)
- jamie: collect full sample list and customer permission for credit (eta: today)

jamie: thumbs up from ACME, will follow up with samples. :thumbsup:

lee: Will add unit test simulating socket FIN + server write and assert classification -> client_abort not 5xx.

ops-bot: Updated incident INC-43210: status=investigating, assigned=[lee,maria], slack-thread=4301234567

maria: If anyone sees similar patterns in europe region, ping me. Might be a general heuristic tweak.

jamie: Filing follow-up: consider adding a small grace window before billing increment when upstream write fails but client FIN detected (to avoid noisy billing on connection reuse).
